tasks.subject: Task 1: `tmux-ctl discord --ops`, `ops-channels`, ops bridge
tasks.description:
**Goal:** The ops bot's state dir is managed by the same subcommands with `--ops`, `ops-channels <cc> <approvals>` writes its config, and `bridge start|stop --ops` runs `bridge.js <_ops dir> --ops`.

**Files:**
- Modify: `tools/lib/discord.zsh` (argument parsing in `discord_cmd`, `_dc_status`, `_dc_bridge`, new `_dc_ops_channels`, `_dc_usage`)
- Modify: `bin/tmux-ctl` (help lines 44–47, and bump the `sed -n '2,NNp'` help range if you add a line — `tmux-ctl help` must still print its last line)
- Modify: `docs/INSTALL.md` (an "Ops bot" section: create a second Discord app, `tmux-ctl discord token --ops`, `pair --ops`, `ops-channels`, Message Content intent not needed, the bot needs `applications.commands` scope)
- Test: `tools/tests/test_ctl_discord_ops.zsh` (new; use `tools/tests/lib.zsh` like `test_ctl_discord_channel.zsh`)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `--ops` selects `$(_dc_root)/_ops` for `token|pair|deny|policy|allow|remove|forget|status|audit|bridge`; `--ops` with `--project` → usage error, rc 2.
- [ ] `tmux-ctl discord ops-channels <cc> <ap>` (both all digits, else usage rc 2; needs an allowlisted user, else "pair or allow a user first" rc 1) writes `<_ops>/bridge.json` `{"command_center","approvals","user"}` mode 600 and adds both ids to `access.json` `groups` with `{"requireMention": false, "allowFrom": [...]}`; a second identical call prints `(unchanged)` and changes no mtime.
- [ ] `status --ops` prints `command center: <id>`, `approvals: <id>` (or `none`), and the bridge line; it does not print `channel:`.
- [ ] `bridge start --ops` starts window `discord-ops` in hidden session `_ops-bg` running `exec node …/bridge.js <_ops dir> --ops`; `--keeper` and `bridge.stopped` behave as for projects; it refuses without a token or without both channel ids.
- [ ] The tokenish-argument guard still applies to every new argument.
- [ ] `tmux-ctl help` output's last line is unchanged (help range bumped if needed).
- [ ] Existing discord zsh suites stay green.

**Verify:** `zsh tools/tests/test_ctl_discord_ops.zsh && zsh tools/tests/test_ctl_discord.zsh && zsh tools/tests/test_ctl_discord_channel.zsh` → each ends with its ok/ALL PASS summary, rc 0

tasks.subject: Task 2: bridge ops mode: card buttons, approvals channel, ke
tasks.description:
**Goal:** `bridge.js <dir> --ops` posts the card with its buttons in #command-center, approval posts with their buttons in #approvals, edits any keyed message, answers read-only buttons from `views.json`, runs the pause-all confirm step, and writes action events.

**Files:**
- Modify: `tools/discord-bridge/bridge.js`
- Modify: `tools/discord-bridge/lib/state.js` (defaults gain `posts: {}`, `approvals: {}`)
- Modify: `tools/discord-bridge/test/fake-client.js` (multiple channels, `reply`/`followUp`/`update` on interactions, components captured)
- Test: `tools/discord-bridge/test/ops.test.js` (new); existing `bridge.test.js` stays green

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `createBridge({dir, client, ops: true})`; `main()` sets `ops` from `--ops` in argv. Project mode behaviour is unchanged (existing tests green).
- [ ] Ops `home()` is `bridge.json.command_center`; `approval` ops go to `bridge.json.approvals`. Card ops in ops mode carry the three-button row (customIds exactly `ab:ops:pause-all`, `ab:ops:resume-all`, `ab:ops:inbox`); the 30 s throttle still applies.
- [ ] `approval` builds the components per kind exactly as in Global Constraints (merge: 3 buttons + a select of ≤ 25 options from `views.json` `evidence[key].files`, option value = path cut to 100 chars; no files → no select row).
- [ ] `post` with `key` records `st.posts[key]`; `edit` finds the key in prompts, posts or approvals, edits the text, sets `components: []`; unknown key logs `edit <key>: no message` and the op is removed.
- [ ] Clicks (allowlisted users only; others get ephemeral `Not authorized.` and a `rejected` event):
  - `ab:ops:inbox` → ephemeral list from `views.json.approvals` (`<project> · <title>` + link per line, `No open decisions.` when empty) and a `read` event;
  - `ab:ops:files:<key>:<page>` → ephemeral (or `update` when clicked from the ephemeral) page of 10 files `path +add -del`, with `Prev`/`Next` buttons (`ab:ops:files:<key>:<n±1>`, omitted at the ends) and `page k/n`; `read` event;
  - `ab:ops:diff:<key>` select → ephemeral reply with `evidence[key].diffs[value]` in a ```diff block (≤ 1800 chars, as written by the board); `read` event;
  - `ab:ops:pause-all` → ephemeral `Pause every running queue?` with one button `Confirm pause all` `ab:ops:pause-all-confirm:<ms now>`; no event besides `read`;
  - `ab:ops:pause-all-confirm:*`, `ab:ops:resume-all`, `ab:ops:allow:*`, `ab:ops:deny:*`, `ab:ops:merge:*`, `ab:ops:keep:*` → `deferUpdate` (or ephemeral `Sent.` for the confirm) and a `click` event with `custom_id`.
  - a missing or unreadable `views.json` → ephemeral `Board data not available yet.`
- [ ] Every reply ≤ 2000 chars, `allowedMentions: {parse: []}`.

**Verify:** `cd tools/discord-bridge && npm test` → `# fail 0`

tasks.subject: Task 3: slash commands and forms (both bridge modes)
tasks.description:
**Goal:** The ops bridge registers `/status /queue /pause /resume /idea /new-spec /approvals` as guild commands in its server and answers them; project bridges register the same set with `project` defaulting to their own project.

**Files:**
- Modify: `tools/discord-bridge/bridge.js`
- Create: `tools/discord-bridge/lib/commands.js` (the registration payload and the per-command handlers, pure where possible)
- Test: `tools/discord-bridge/test/commands.test.js` (new)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] On ready, `client.application.commands.set(payload, guildId)` once per connection with guildId = the guild of `command_center` (ops) or of the home channel (project). Payload: 7 chat-input commands; `project` is a string option, required for `queue pause resume idea new-spec` in ops mode, optional in project mode and for `status`. A registration failure is logged and does not stop the bridge.
- [ ] Each command checks `allowFrom` first (else ephemeral `Not authorized.` + `rejected` event).
- [ ] `/status [project]` → `views.status._all` or `views.status[project]`; `/queue <project>` → `views.queue[project]` in a code block; `/approvals` → the same list as the Inbox button. Each writes a `read` event. Unknown project → ephemeral `Unknown project: <name>` (no event besides `read`).
- [ ] `/pause` `/resume` → ephemeral `Sent to <project>.` and a `slash` event `{command, project}`.
- [ ] `/idea` → `showModal` custom_id `ab:modal:idea:<project>`, inputs `title` (short, ≤ 100) and `text` (paragraph, ≤ 1000); `/new-spec` → `ab:modal:new-spec:<project>`, inputs `what` (short) and `why` (paragraph). Submit → `modal` event with the trimmed fields and ephemeral `💡 noted for <project>` (idea) / `Sent to <project>'s lead.` (new-spec).
- [ ] Project mode reads `views.json` from `path.join(path.dirname(dir), '_ops', 'views.json')`; when absent, read commands answer `Ops bot not set up (tmux-ctl discord ops-channels).`; action commands still work (they go to the project's own events dir).
- [ ] No command takes or runs a command line (no free-form option besides the form fields, which are only written into the event).

**Verify:** `cd tools/discord-bridge && npm test` → `# fail 0`

tasks.subject: Task 4: `board/discord_ops.py`: card, views, decision mirror
tasks.description:
**Goal:** One module that, given the overview records and each project's lead tasks, renders the command-center card, writes `views.json`, mirrors decisions into #approvals and critical events into #command-center, edits both copies on resolution, and consumes the ops (and forwarded project) events. **Files:** - Create: `board/discord_ops.py` - Modify: `board/tc_env.py` (`ops_dir()`) - Modify: `board/discord_feed.py` (`_check`: `approval` op, `post.key`; `ops_for_events`: decision-tier posts get `key = "dec:" + sha1(ts|text)[:12]`, `merge_approval` posts get `key = "merge:"`) - Modify: `board/discord_controls.py` (`scan_prompts`: when `discord_ops.configured()`, also `discord_ops.mirror_prompt(project, key, window, tool, lines)`; `_edit`: also `discord_ops.resolve(project, key, text)`; `consume_events`: `slash`/`modal`/`read`/`rejected` events go to `discord_ops.handle_event(project, d, ev, add_line, allow)`) - Test: `board/tests/test_discord_ops.py` (new); `test_discord_feed.py`, `test_discord_controls.py` stay green **Acceptance Criteria:** - [ ] `render_card(records, tasks_by_project, links, limits, now)` → ≤ 1900 chars, plain text (no code block, so links render): header `usage: 5h

% · week

% · today $` (`—` for unknown parts); one line per project `**** · · / · blockers: · waiting on you: · <>` (link from the project's `bridge.json.channel` + `bridge-state.json.guild_id`; omitted when unknown); `updated HH:MM` last; overflow cut with `… more`. Fixture test with two projects + one 40-project overflow test. - [ ] `tick(records, tasks_by_project, limits, now, add_line)` under `flock(<_ops>/ops-state.lock)` (non-blocking; returns None when held): writes the card op when due (`discord_feed.card_op_due`), writes `views.json` atomically (shape in Global Constraints; `queue[p]` = `queue_text(lead_tasks)`: the `discord_feed._queue` line, then one line per `Plan & run:` task in id order, `✓`/`▶`/`·` + `discord_feed._spec_name(subject)` + ` — ` when set, cut to 1800 chars), reads each project's feed from its own offset in `ops-state.json` (first sight: offset = file size, no replay), and per event: tier `decision` → one `approval` op (kind `merge` for `merge_approval`, else `other`, with the project-channel link), tier `critical` → one ops `post` with `mention_user: true` prefixed `: `. - [ ] Lead questions: a project whose record `needs_you` holds window `claude` gets one `approval` (kind `question`, text `: the lead is waiting on you`, link to the project channel); when it leaves `needs_you`, `edit` → `: answered`. Not re-posted while it stays. - [ ] `mirror_prompt` posts kind `perm` (`🔐 · wants to run ` + the first 15 lines in a code block); `resolve(project, src_key, text)` edits the ops copy with `: ` and drops it from `views.approvals`. Both no-ops when ops is not configured. - [ ] Ops events (`consume(add_line, run, now)`), allowlist re-read per event; each audited in `<_ops>/audit.jsonl`: - `ab:ops:allow|deny:` → a `perm` event `{key: , choice: allow|deny, user, ts}` written into that project's `events/` (the controls step presses and edits both copies) — audited `forwarded`; - `ab:ops:pause-all-confirm:` → within 60 s of ``: the pause line to every project whose queue state is running (audited `queued `), else `expired`; `ab:ops:resume-all` → the resume line to every paused project; - `ab:ops:merge:` / `ab:ops:keep:` → `discord_merge.on_merge(...)` / keep line (Task 5 provides `on_merge`; until then the test injects a stub); - `slash` pause/resume → that project's line; `modal` idea → `ideas.add(project, title, detail=text)`, new-spec → `[Discord] new spec request: — ` (whitespace collapsed, each ≤ 300 chars); `read` → audited `answered`; `rejected` → audited `rejected`; unknown project → audited `unknown project`. - The same `handle_event` serves events forwarded from a project's `consume_events` (project defaulted to that project). - [ ] Delivery semantics (tests for each): a repeated event file (same content twice) presses/sends once per file only — pause-all lines are idempotent for the lead; a duplicated `ab:ops:allow` after the first is answered by the controls' existing `unknown` path (no second press); events are processed in filename order; a decision already mirrored is never posted twice (keys in `ops-state.json.mirrored`, newest 2000). - [ ] Ops not configured (`<_ops>/bridge.json` missing) → `tick` and `consume` return without writing anything; project behaviour unchanged. **Verify:** `python3 -m unittest board.tests.test_discord_ops board.tests.test_discord_feed board.tests.test_discord_controls` → `OK` ```json:metadata {"files": ["board/discord_ops.py", "board/tc_env.py", "board/discord_feed.py", "board/discord_controls.py", "board/tests/test_discord_ops.py"], "verifyCommand": "python3 -m unittest board.tests.test_discord_ops board.tests.test_discord_feed board.tests.test_discord_controls", "acceptanceCriteria": ["render_card format and <=1900 cap with overflow", "tick: card when due, views.json atomic, per-project feed offsets without replay, decision->approval, critical->ops post", "lead question approval posted once and edited answered", "mirror_prompt/resolve edit ops copy; no-op unconfigured", "ops events: allow/deny forwarded, pause-all confirm 60s, resume-all, merge/keep, slash, modal idea/new-spec, read, rejected, all audited", "delivery: repeats, order, no double mirror", "unconfigured -> nothing written"], "modelTier": "standard"} ```

tasks.subject: Task 5: merge evidence and `tmux-ctl discord merge-request`
tasks.description:
**Goal:** A lead in queue mode with `integration: ask` runs one command that computes the merge evidence, posts the decision, and a later Merge tap re-checks the branch tip before telling the lead to merge. **Files:** - Create: `board/discord_merge.py` (`evidence(repo, branch, target) -> dict`, `request(project, repo, task, spec, branch, target, tests, verdict, findings, now)`, `on_merge(project, ev_key, state, add_line, now)`, CLI `main()` for the zsh wrapper) - Modify: `tools/lib/discord.zsh` (`merge-request` subcommand → `python3 -I board/discord_merge.py request …`) - Modify: `bin/tmux-ctl` (one help line; bump the help `sed` range) - Modify: `board/discord_ops.py` (call `discord_merge.on_merge` for `ab:ops:merge:*`; views evidence from `<_ops>/evidence/*.json`) - Test: `board/tests/test_discord_merge.py` (new, with a fixture git repo built in a temp dir); `tools/tests/test_ctl_discord_ops.zsh` gains the CLI case **Acceptance Criteria:** - [ ] `tmux-ctl discord merge-request --project

--task --spec --branch [--target main] --tests "" --verdict "" [--finding ""]…` (repo = the caller's git toplevel; `--repo` overrides) writes `<_ops>/evidence/

-.json` and appends one feed event `{kind: "merge_approval", tier: "decision", spec, text, refs: {task, evidence, sha}}` to the project's feed; prints `merge-request: posted `; rc 0. Without ops configured it still posts in the project channel (the feed event) and says `(ops bot not set up: project channel only)`. - [ ] Evidence: `sha` = `git rev-parse `; `files` from `git diff --numstat ...` (binary `-` counts as 0); post text = `merge approval: ` / ` → @ ` / `git diff --stat` lines, first 25 files then `… more` / `tests: ` / `final review: ` / one line per finding (each cut to 200 chars) / `diff: files, + −`; text cut to 1900. `diffs[path]` = `git diff ... -- ` cut to 1800 + `\n… too long, see board`. - [ ] Fixture test: a repo with 30 changed files → 25 stat lines + `… 5 more`; a binary file; a diff of > 1800 chars carries the note. - [ ] `on_merge`: re-runs `git rev-parse `; equal to evidence `sha` → `[Discord] merge approved for ` to the lead and edits both copies to `merge approved — sent to the lead`; different or branch gone → edits both copies to `branch changed since this was posted`, then calls `request(...)` again with the stored fields (fresh evidence, fresh post). Keep → `[Discord] keep branch for `, edits `kept: `. A second tap on a resolved key → audited `unknown`, nothing sent. - [ ] No branch/target/spec value reaches a shell string: every git call is an argv list with `--` before paths; branch and target must match `^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$` and not start with `-` (else rc 2, nothing written). **Verify:** `python3 -m unittest board.tests.test_discord_merge board.tests.test_discord_ops && zsh tools/tests/test_ctl_discord_ops.zsh` → `OK` and the zsh suite's pass line ```json:metadata {"files": ["board/discord_merge.py", "tools/lib/discord.zsh", "bin/tmux-ctl", "board/discord_ops.py", "board/tests/test_discord_merge.py", "tools/tests/test_ctl_discord_ops.zsh"], "verifyCommand": "python3 -m unittest board.tests.test_discord_merge board.tests.test_discord_ops && zsh tools/tests/test_ctl_discord_ops.zsh", "acceptanceCriteria": ["merge-request writes evidence json and one merge_approval decision feed event; project-only note without ops", "evidence text format, 25-file cut, binary, diff 1800 cut", "on_merge sha equal -> lead line + both edited; mismatch -> branch changed + fresh request; keep; second tap unknown", "argv-only git, branch/target shape check"], "modelTier": "standard"} ```

tasks.subject: Task 6: Queue mode `integration: ask` in the lead rules
tasks.description:
**Goal:** The lead rules know the new `ask` integration: finish up to the merge, keep the branch, post the decision with `tmux-ctl discord merge-request`, move on; merge or keep later when the `[Discord]` line arrives. **Files:** - Modify: `claude/orchestrator.md` (§ Queue mode: step 1's integration list and `metadata.queue.integration` values gain `ask`, "approve from the phone"; step 2 gains one sentence for `ask`; a new bullet for the two `[Discord] merge approved for ` / `[Discord] keep branch for ` lines) - Test: `tools/tests/test_orchestrator_rules.zsh` if it exists, else `tools/tests/test_queue_ask_rule.zsh` (new): greps that the three texts are present **Acceptance Criteria:** - [ ] `claude/orchestrator.md` names `"ask"` in the `metadata.queue.integration` value list, and step 2 says, verbatim in substance: with `ask`, run `finishing-a-development-branch` up to the integration step with the option "keep the branch", then `tmux-ctl discord merge-request --project

--task --spec --branch --tests "" --verdict "" [--finding …]`, record `metadata.outcome = "awaiting merge approval "`, and start the next spec. - [ ] On `[Discord] merge approved for `: run `finishing-a-development-branch` with `merge` for that spec's branch (its pre-merge tests and live-checkout checks run), update the task's outcome to `merged `; on `[Discord] keep branch for `: outcome `kept `. Neither line is ever a push. - [ ] The sentence fits the file's style (no new headings); the test greps for `"ask"`, `merge-request`, and `merge approved for`. **Verify:** `zsh tools/tests/test_queue_ask_rule.zsh` → `ok` lines, rc 0 ```json:metadata {"files": ["claude/orchestrator.md", "tools/tests/test_queue_ask_rule.zsh"], "verifyCommand": "zsh tools/tests/test_queue_ask_rule.zsh", "acceptanceCriteria": ["ask in integration values; step 2 ask flow with merge-request and outcome awaiting merge approval", "merge approved -> finishing with merge, outcome merged; keep -> kept; never a push", "grep test for ask, merge-request, merge approved for"], "modelTier": "mechanical"} ```

tasks.subject: Task 8: daily digest
tasks.description:
**Goal:** At `TC_DISCORD_DIGEST_AT` (default `08:00` local, `off` disables) the board posts one digest in #command-center covering everything since the last digest. **Files:** - Create: `board/discord_digest.py` (`due(state, now, at)`, `build(projects, feeds, approvals, records, limits, since, now) -> str`, `tick(records, limits, now)`) - Modify: `board/server.py` (call `discord_digest.tick` next to the ops tick, same error wrapping) - Test: `board/tests/test_discord_digest.py` (new) **Acceptance Criteria:** - [ ] `due`: true once per local day at or after `at` (`HH:MM`); state `<_ops>/digest-state.json {"last_ts", "last_day"}`; first ever run uses `since = now - 86400`; `off` → never; an unparsable value → default `08:00` and one stderr line. - [ ] Content: header `digest · 5h

% · week

% · spend $`; per project with activity: `: merged () · failed () · running · decisions · test runs failed `, specs cut to 3 names + `…`; decisions with links as following lines; a project with nothing new → `: quiet`. Sources: feed events since `since` (`spec_outcome` text `merged…`/`failed…`, `spec_started`, kind `test_failed`), open approvals from `ops-state.json`, `spend_today` from records. ≤ 1900 chars, cut with `… more projects`. - [ ] One ops `post` op (tier `progress`, no mention) per digest; never posts twice the same day (test with two ticks); a feed spanning midnight counts events from both days (aged fixture: events dated yesterday 23:50 and today 00:10 with `since` yesterday 08:00). - [ ] Critical events are not held: the digest never suppresses Task 4's critical posts (test: a critical event before the digest is still posted by `discord_ops.tick`). - [ ] Ops not configured → nothing. **Verify:** `python3 -m unittest board.tests.test_discord_digest` → `OK` ```json:metadata {"files": ["board/discord_digest.py", "board/server.py", "board/tests/test_discord_digest.py"], "verifyCommand": "python3 -m unittest board.tests.test_discord_digest", "acceptanceCriteria": ["due once per local day at TC_DISCORD_DIGEST_AT; off; bad value default", "content lines, quiet, cut <=1900", "one post per day; midnight-spanning feed counted", "critical not held", "unconfigured nothing"], "modelTier": "standard"} ```

tasks.subject: Task 9: ops chat goes to the overseer
tasks.description:
**Goal:** When the ops token exists, the overseer Claude starts with the Discord channel on and `DISCORD_STATE_DIR=<_ops dir>`, so the user can chat with it in #command-center; it keeps its read-only rules.

**Files:**
- Modify: `bin/claude-overseer`
- Modify: `claude/overseer.md` (two lines: messages from Discord arrive as channel tags; answer with the discord `reply` tool; it still has no authority and points to the buttons/slash commands for actions)
- Modify: `claude/overseer-settings.json` only if the probe shows the discord plugin's tools need an allow entry (read-only reply/fetch only; never access tools)
